_comment: Which FINGERS a grasp uses. Loaded by simulation/grasp_config_builder.load_finger_config(). The value IS the list -- there is no name to look up, because a named alias like 'tripod' carries no information its list does not, while costing a lookup and a naming decision every time a new combination is wanted.
_comment_order: ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING, not a set. Contact SLOTS are positional in the NLP: slot 1 = p1, slot 2 = p2, slot 3 = p3, slot 4 = p4. Slot 1 is what the antipodal seed march starts from (_seed_pair marches ALONG contact 1's inward normal), and w_align is gated to slot-1<->slot-2 opposition. So ['thumb','middle'] and ['middle','thumb'] are DIFFERENT problems -- the first finger anchors the grasp.
_comment_roles: Each entry must be a key of kinova_common.constants.FINGER_TIP_SITES / FINGER_CODE (index, middle, ring, thumb), which own the model's site and geom naming. This file never repeats a site name, so it cannot drift from the model. 2 to 4 fingers; the NLP has four contact slots. Slot 4 (the ring finger) shares slot 2's quadratic patch exactly as slot 3 does, so a four-finger entry puts THREE fingertips on one patch -- see GraspConfig3D.c4_patch_offset_m before adding one.
_comment_measured: MEASURED 2026-09-12, seed 0, plan-only, 80/3 GWS preset, five tabletop objects. ['thumb','middle'] is the same NLP with slot 2 re-bound: committed p2 moves from 19.0mm off the index tip to 16.1mm off the middle tip (017_orange) with grasp span preserved (67.8 -> 68.0mm). All ten 2-finger cells certify wrench-feasible, but thumb+middle is uniformly WEAKER -- gamma_min rises on every object, by 4.9x on 036_wood_block (3.08 -> 14.93 N against a 25 N ceiling). w_align and the seed priors are tuned for thumb+index.

per_object._comment: Overrides the default list for one YCB id. Read by load_finger_config() and consulted by BOTH the benchmark and the live teleop, so an object grasps the same way in either. Shape drives the choice: a SPHEROID is fully constrained by an antipodal pinch and a third contact only adds a finger to collide with, while a BOX has flat faces where the third contact buys a real off-axis moment arm.
per_object._comment_measured: MEASURED 2026-09-14, 6 objects x 3 seeds x 2 arms, full execution, force-closure criterion (every finger loaded + real lift). Tripod 3/3 on 009_gelatin_box and 3/3 on 036_wood_block; tripod 0/3 on all three spheroids (014_lemon, 017_orange, 056_tennis_ball) where the pinch is 3/3, 3/3, 3/3. The spheroids still reach the bin at n=3 (5/9) but as a CAGING grasp with one finger unloaded -- task success without force closure.
per_object._comment_mug: 025_mug is left on the PINCH. It is the one object that fails both ways (1/3 either arm) and its failure is upstream of the finger count: the seeder puts the thumb contact on the RIM, pressing straight down (outward normal +z) while the other fingers push sideways, and solve_gamma_live correctly refuses that geometry. Adding a finger does not fix a contact that is in the wrong place.
